"""Single-tactic experiments on top of the baseline: each variant changes one thing, so a benchmark run
shows what that tactic alone is worth against the supplier bots (results: docs/benchmarks/).
  lowball    a deeper opening anchor: ask for less than we need, so the middle lands in our favour
  questions  three questions in every e-mail: make answering us more work than agreeing
  polite     a warm, appreciative tone
  shelby     a curt, hard tone with a threat to place the order elsewhere
  budget     a ceiling set by a third party ("management released at most EUR X") that we do not cross
  trade      no price move without a move from the supplier, and said so: every option is a trade
Everything else - term sheets from C, arguments, holding and closing - is the baseline's.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from negotiator.session import Negotiation
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import GOAL_ANCHOR, BaselineStrategy, SupplierPlan
from negotiator.telemetry import log
# tone -> (first e-mail, later e-mails, closing line or None)
TONES = {
    "polite": (
        "thank you very much for your quote and for the good cooperation - we appreciate the work your team puts "
        "into it. We would like to find a solution that works for both sides; as it stands the quote is above what "
        "we can accept.",
        "thank you for your reply and for moving towards us - we appreciate it. We have moved as well and hope you "
        "can take a further step.",
        "Thank you for your support - we are confident we will find an agreement.",
    ),
    "shelby": (
        "we have read your quote. It is not a number we will sign.",
        "you have moved a little. It is not enough. We have moved too, and we do not move twice for nothing.",
        "This order will be placed either way - with you or without you. Your move.",
    ),
}
QUESTIONS = [
    "What lead time can you commit to for the first call-off?",
    "Which share of your price is material, and which index does it follow?",
    "How much free capacity do you have for this part in the coming quarter?",
    "Who on your side has to approve a price below your quote?",
    "Would faster payment or a longer commitment help you more?",
    "What defect rate do you achieve on comparable parts?",
    "What would a higher annual volume change in your calculation?",
    "Which Incoterm and packaging are cheapest for you?",
    "Can you hold the price for the whole term without an index clause?",
]
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tactic:
    name: str
    anchor_scale: float = 1.0  # multiplies the baseline's anchor per category goal
    tone: str | None = None  # a key of TONES; None: the baseline's wording
    questions_per_round: int = 0
    budget_share: float | None = None  # ceiling = target + share x (opening - target); None: no ceiling
    conditional: bool = False  # the supplier does not move -> we do not move at all
TACTICS = {
    t.name: t
    for t in (
        Tactic("lowball", anchor_scale=1.5),
        Tactic("questions", questions_per_round=3),
        Tactic("polite", tone="polite"),
        Tactic("shelby", tone="shelby"),
        Tactic("budget", budget_share=0.5),
        Tactic("trade", conditional=True),
    )
}
class ExperimentStrategy(BaselineStrategy):
    def __init__(self, tactic: Tactic, data=None, llm=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(data, llm)
        self.tactic = tactic
        self.name = tactic.name
        self.ceilings: dict[str, float] = {}
    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
        super().prepare(neg)
        tac = self.tactic
        goal = neg.buyer.get("category_goal", "leverage")
        current = neg.buyer.get("current_unit_price")
        for sid, plan in self.plans.items():
            if plan.open_price is None or plan.target_price is None:
                continue
            if tac.anchor_scale != 1.0:
                base = min(plan.open_price, current) if current else plan.open_price
                target = base * (1 - GOAL_ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.06) * tac.anchor_scale)
                plan.target_price = round(min(max(target, plan.floor_price or 0.0), plan.open_price), 2)
            if tac.budget_share is not None:
                gap = plan.open_price - plan.target_price
                self.ceilings[sid] = round(plan.target_price + tac.budget_share * gap, 2)
            neg.recorder.event(
                "experiment",
                session_id=neg.session_id,
                case_id=neg.case_id,
                supplier_id=sid,
                tactic=tac.name,
                target_price=plan.target_price,
                ceiling=self.ceilings.get(sid),
            )
            log.info("%s %s: target %s ceiling %s", sid, tac.name, plan.target_price, self.ceilings.get(sid))
    def _next_price(self, plan: SupplierPlan, theirs, ours, round_index, their_path=None) -> float:
        price = super()._next_price(plan, theirs, ours, round_index, their_path)
        if self.tactic.conditional and ours and their_path and len(their_path) >= 2:
            if their_path[-1] >= their_path[-2]:
                price = ours[-1]
        ceiling = self.ceilings.get(plan.supplier_id)
        if ceiling is not None:
            price = min(price, max(ceiling, ours[-1] if ours else 0.0))
        return price
    def _opener(self, first: bool) -> str:
        if self.tactic.tone is None:
            return super()._opener(first)
        return TONES[self.tactic.tone][0 if first else 1]
    def _extra_lines(self, neg: Negotiation, plan: SupplierPlan, first: bool) -> list[str]:
        tac, lines = self.tactic, []
        ceiling = self.ceilings.get(plan.supplier_id)
        if ceiling is not None:
            lines.append(
                f"Our management has released a fixed budget for this part: EUR {ceiling:,.2f} per unit on the terms "
                "of option A is the most I am allowed to sign."
                if first
                else f"The budget ceiling of EUR {ceiling:,.2f} per unit on the terms of option A stands; I cannot "
                "sign above it."
            )

"""Single-tactic experiments on top of the baseline: each variant changes one thing, so a benchmark run
shows what that tactic alone is worth against the supplier bots (results: docs/benchmarks/).
  lowball    a deeper opening anchor: ask for less than we need, so the middle lands in our favour
  questions  three questions in every e-mail: make answering us more work than agreeing
  polite     a warm, appreciative tone
  shelby     a curt, hard tone with a threat to place the order elsewhere
  budget     a ceiling set by a third party ("management released at most EUR X") that we do not cross
  trade      no price move without a move from the supplier, and said so: every option is a trade
Everything else - term sheets from C, arguments, holding and closing - is the baseline's.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from negotiator.session import Negotiation
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import GOAL_ANCHOR, BaselineStrategy, SupplierPlan
from negotiator.telemetry import log
# tone -> (first e-mail, later e-mails, closing line or None)
TONES = {
    "polite": (
        "thank you very much for your quote and for the good cooperation - we appreciate the work your team puts "
        "into it. We would like to find a solution that works for both sides; as it stands the quote is above what "
        "we can accept.",
        "thank you for your reply and for moving towards us - we appreciate it. We have moved as well and hope you "
        "can take a further step.",
        "Thank you for your support - we are confident we will find an agreement.",
    ),
    "shelby": (
        "we have read your quote. It is not a number we will sign.",
        "you have moved a little. It is not enough. We have moved too, and we do not move twice for nothing.",
        "This order will be placed either way - with you or without you. Your move.",
    ),
}
QUESTIONS = [
    "What lead time can you commit to for the first call-off?",
    "Which share of your price is material, and which index does it follow?",
    "How much free capacity do you have for this part in the coming quarter?",
    "Who on your side has to approve a price below your quote?",
    "Would faster payment or a longer commitment help you more?",
    "What defect rate do you achieve on comparable parts?",
    "What would a higher annual volume change in your calculation?",
    "Which Incoterm and packaging are cheapest for you?",
    "Can you hold the price for the whole term without an index clause?",
]
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tactic:
    name: str
    anchor_scale: float = 1.0  # multiplies the baseline's anchor per category goal
    tone: str | None = None  # a key of TONES; None: the baseline's wording
    questions_per_round: int = 0
    budget_share: float | None = None  # ceiling = target + share x (opening - target); None: no ceiling
    conditional: bool = False  # the supplier does not move -> we do not move at all
TACTICS = {
    t.name: t
    for t in (
        Tactic("lowball", anchor_scale=1.5),
        Tactic("questions", questions_per_round=3),
        Tactic("polite", tone="polite"),
        Tactic("shelby", tone="shelby"),
        Tactic("budget", budget_share=0.5),
        Tactic("trade", conditional=True),
    )
}
class ExperimentStrategy(BaselineStrategy):
    def __init__(self, tactic: Tactic, data=None, llm=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(data, llm)
        self.tactic = tactic
        self.name = tactic.name
        self.ceilings: dict[str, float] = {}
    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
        super().prepare(neg)
        tac = self.tactic
        goal = neg.buyer.get("category_goal", "leverage")
        current = neg.buyer.get("current_unit_price")
        for sid, plan in self.plans.items():
            if plan.open_price is None or plan.target_price is None:
                continue
            if tac.anchor_scale != 1.0:
                base = min(plan.open_price, current) if current else plan.open_price
                target = base * (1 - GOAL_ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.06) * tac.anchor_scale)
                plan.target_price = round(min(max(target, plan.floor_price or 0.0), plan.open_price), 2)
            if tac.budget_share is not None:
                gap = plan.open_price - plan.target_price
                self.ceilings[sid] = round(plan.target_price + tac.budget_share * gap, 2)
            neg.recorder.event(
                "experiment",
                session_id=neg.session_id,
                case_id=neg.case_id,
                supplier_id=sid,
                tactic=tac.name,
                target_price=plan.target_price,
                ceiling=self.ceilings.get(sid),
            )
            log.info("%s %s: target %s ceiling %s", sid, tac.name, plan.target_price, self.ceilings.get(sid))
    def _next_price(self, plan: SupplierPlan, theirs, ours, round_index, their_path=None) -> float:
        price = super()._next_price(plan, theirs, ours, round_index, their_path)
        if self.tactic.conditional and ours and their_path and len(their_path) >= 2:
            if their_path[-1] >= their_path[-2]:
                price = ours[-1]
        ceiling = self.ceilings.get(plan.supplier_id)
        if ceiling is not None:
            price = min(price, max(ceiling, ours[-1] if ours else 0.0))
        return price
    def _opener(self, first: bool) -> str:
        if self.tactic.tone is None:
            return super()._opener(first)
        return TONES[self.tactic.tone][0 if first else 1]
    def _extra_lines(self, neg: Negotiation, plan: SupplierPlan, first: bool) -> list[str]:
        tac, lines = self.tactic, []
        ceiling = self.ceilings.get(plan.supplier_id)

"""Does the agent read a case brief correctly? Offline: no arena call, no session, no practice quota.

Each variant (brief_variants.py: the recorded cases and changed copies of them) goes through the step where
`tactical` digests a case - `prepare` - and through the construction of its first e-mail, and what the agent
derived is compared with answers computed with `arena_kit.cost` alone:

  - C of the opening (`c_open`), C of the alternative (`c_alt`), the must-have verdict of each opening;
  - the plan: finite numbers in a sensible order (target <= upper <= opening, upper <= alternative);
  - the first ask: a valid term sheet (exactly the negotiable fields, allowed values, must-haves kept), a
    positive price not above the opening's, cheaper for us than the opening, and for a relationship goal not
    below the strategy's own floor;
  - an unknown `type`, `category_goal` or field: no crash, a default policy, no relationship charge.

It judges the reading of a brief, not the strategy: no supplier answers here. A finding that is a known fault of
the agent turns the variant into an xfail with its reason (KNOWN); anything else fails. Without recorded sessions
(`runs/` is not in the repository) the module skips.
"""

import json
import math
import traceback
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from arena_kit.cost import OPS, closing_terms, total_cost
from brief_variants import OFF_DATA, Variant, build_negotiation, expected, load_bases, sheet_faults, variants

from negotiator.guards import accept_problems, clean_message, sheet_problems
from negotiator.strategy import TacticalStrategy
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import SANE_PRICE

RUNS = PACKAGE_ROOT / "runs"
BASES = load_bases(RUNS) if RUNS.is_dir() else {}
VARIANTS = variants(BASES) if BASES else []
EUR = 0.011  # C is rounded to cents

# Finding code -> the fault of the agent behind it. A variant whose findings are all listed here is an xfail;
# when the fault is fixed the finding disappears and the variant passes. "verified": the arena's own records or
# its published rules show the agent is wrong. "suspicion": a brief outside what api.md describes, where the
# agent's reaction is doubtful but nothing recorded says what the arena would do.
KNOWN: dict[str, str] = {

|---|---|

## Result and cost

| Run | Strategy | D01 score | D01 C_deal (EUR) | D02 score | D02 C_deal (EUR) | Mean | Rounds D01 / D02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `20261010-214628-sandbox-tactical-slow25` | `tactical-slow25` | 0.957 | 410,370 | 0.671 | 175,688 | **0.814** | 5 / 10 |
| `20261010-214434-sandbox-tactical` | `tactical` (control, same commit) | 0.969 | 409,883 | 0.587 | 180,520 | 0.778 | 5 / 10 |

Sandbox: D01 (price increase, stabilise; C_open 448,811, C_best 408,624) and D02 (RFQ with two suppliers, leverage;
C_open 214,296, C_best 156,739). Run cost: 0 practice sessions, 0 LLM tokens, about 2 minutes wall time per run.
Practice: see the section at the end.

## Strategy

`strategy/patient.py`, strategy name `tactical-slow25`, commit `556a31d` plus the uncommitted `patient.py`.
`tactical` with one change: our step towards the supplier is a quarter of what `tactical` would take, and at least
the minimum step of 0.4 % of C.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `scale` | 0.25 (`tactical-slow50`: 0.5, played on the simulator only) |
| everything else | `tactical` as on `556a31d` |

## Notes

- The change comes from [`../backlog.md`](../backlog.md) 2.1: on practice case P18 the supplier agreed as soon as our
  rising offer reached what it would take (5.00 → 5.25 → 5.50).
- D02 gained 0.084, D01 lost 0.012. One run each on two demo cases.
- **The simulator pointed the same way before the sandbox run.** `negotiator sim bench tactical tactical-slow50
  tactical-slow25 --reps 5`, fitted on all sessions up to 21:40: D02 0.54 → 0.66, D01 0.84 → 0.85. For the ten
  practice cases it gave a mean of 0.618 for `tactical` and 0.644 for `tactical-slow25`, with P02 0.34 → 0.51,
  P05 0.53 → 0.60 and P08 0.52 → 0.38. Those are simulator figures, not arena results; its error on single practice
  cases was 0.1 to 0.35 against the arena run of the same evening.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.
